Report Highlights:   
Posts forecasts MY 25/26 cotton production at 6.35 million metric tons (MMT) on stable planted area 
and a return to normal weather conditions. Imports are forecast at 1.55 MMT and domestic consumption 
at 8.15 MMT. Post revised up its estimate for MY 24/25 cotton production to 6.81 MMT. MY 24/25 
imports are revised down to 1.40 MMT, as a glut of domestic cotton and high MY 23/24 imports are 
reducing demand for imported cotton. Beijing’s imposition of 140 percent tariffs on U.S. cotton will all 
but stop further imports from the United States.

2 
 
FAS China provides this analysis and reporting as a service to the United States agricultural 
community, and to our farmers, ranchers, rural communities, and agribusiness operations in 
support of a worldwide agricultural information system and a level playing field for U.S. 
agriculture. 
 
Executive Summary 
 
Post forecasts MY 25/26 cotton production at 6.35 MMT, down five percent on a return to trend 
yields after last season’s excellent weather. The Chinese government will continue its target 
price-based subsidy for Xinjiang cotton to maintain planted area and production in that region for 
2025. In contrast, production outside Xinjiang is expected to decline further due to limited 
subsidies, lower cotton prices, reduced quality, higher input costs, and competition from 
alternative crops.  
 
Cotton consumption for MY 25/26 is forecast at 8.15 MMT on anticipated domestic economic 
growth as Beijing seeks to stimulate domestic consumption, and Chinese textile and apparel 
companies seek additional export destinations for their products. China continues to subsidize 
the movement of the yarn-spinning and textile industry into Xinjiang out of other regions. Cotton 
imports for MY 25/26 are projected at 1.55 MMT, up slightly from the low levels estimated for 
MY 24/25.  
 
Post revised its MY 24/25 cotton production estimate upward to 6.81 MMT compared to an 
estimated 5.90 MMT for MY 23/24. Favorable weather conditions during the crop growing and 
harvesting season in Xinjiang province contributed to better-than-expected yields, which resulted 
in a significantly higher volume of classified and ginned cotton in the region. Xinjiang’s share of 
China’s cotton production reached a record of 92.3 percent in MY 24/25, up from the 90.9 
percent in the previous marketing year, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). 
This higher level of production combined with elevated imports in MY 23/24 has led to large 
stocks and reduced China’s appetite for imported cotton. For MY 24/25, Post revises its import 
forecasts down 22 percent, to 1.40 MMT, a 57 percent decline from MY 23/24. Additionally, 
tariffs imposed on U.S. cotton – 15 percent in March and an additional 125 percent in April 2025 
– are expected all but stop cotton imports from the United States.  
 
China’s textile and apparel exports in 2024 grew by 2.8 percent year-on-year, driven by 
improved global market conditions during the last quarter of the year. Export levels remained 
stable from August to September but gained momentum in the last three months of 2024. During 
the first seven months of MY 24/25, China’s cumulative export of textiles and apparel were 
$174.3 billion, a year-on-year increase of 2 percent. However, ongoing trade disputes and market 
uncertainty are expected to lead to a decline in textile and apparel exports for the remainder of 
MY 24/25. Tariffs will reduce Chinese textile exports to the United States. Post lowered its 
estimates for MY 24/25 consumption to 8.05 MMT. However, competitive domestic cotton 
prices will bolster the domestic spinning industry, and stimulative policies are expected to help 
support domestic demand for textile and apparel products in the latter half of the marketing year.

3 
 
Production 
 
Post forecasts MY 25/26 cotton production at 6.35 MMT, a decrease of 5 percent from the 
current marketing year, due to stable planted area and a return to trend for yield. Planted area is 
projected to remain almost unchanged at 2.93 million hectares (Mha), supported by the 
continuation of the 18,600 yuan/metric ton ($2,660/MT) target price-based subsidy for Xinjiang 
cotton, which is sufficient to incentivize continued planting by Xinjiang farmers as it will ensure 
profitability with current production margins. Last year’s near-perfect weather resulted in higher-
than-normal yields and Post’s forecast assumes a return to average weather conditions.  About 
96-98 percent of cotton grown in Xinjiang is upland cotton, with only 2-4 percent being long-
staple cotton. 
 
Post raised its estimates for MY 24/25 cotton production to 6.81 MMT, up 0.6 MMT from the 
previous report Cotton and Products Update CH2024-0156 due to the higher than expected 
yields in Xinjiang. Post’s estimate is 160,000 MT lower than the official USDA estimate, based 
primarily on generally lower estimates publicly available sources and industry contacts.  
 
NBS data released in January estimated MY24/25 cotton production at 6.16 MMT, a year-on-
year increase of 546,000 MT or 9.7 percent. Xinjiang contributed approximately 92.3 percent, 
5.69 MMT, of the total output and saw an 11.4 year-on-year percent increase. Total planted area 
of cotton was 2.84 Mha, with a national average unit yield of 2,171.6 kg/ha, which is 156.7 kg/ha 
or 7.8 percentage points higher than 2023. The NBS cotton production survey approach uses 
remote sensing and sampling for major production areas (i.e., Xinjiang), while employing 
comprehensive statistics for non-major areas. However, different methods used in Xinjiang 
versus other regions might lead to inconsistencies in data quality and comparability. 
 
The China Cotton Association (CCA) raised its production estimate for MY24/25 cotton to 6.44 
MMT, given higher estimates for planted area (2.91 Mha) and yield (2,212.19 kg/ha). CCA’s 
estimates for Xinjiang cotton production is 6.1 MMT, a year-on-year increase of 10.8 percent and 
accounting for 94.8 percent of the national output. Over 99.9 percent of the harvested cotton had 
been traded by the end of March.  
 
The China National Cotton Exchange (CNCE) is an official organization that operates a trading 
platform open to its members. CNCE publishes regular data on ginned cotton volumes.  
According to CNCE, as of January 23 2025, MY24/25 Xinjiang ginned cotton volume reached 
6.39 MMT accumulatively, a year-over-year increase of 18.9 percent. Industry contacts expect 
Xinjiang ginned cotton volumes to further increase, given the ginning trend in the previous two 
to three years. Of the total ginned cotton, Xinjiang Production and Construction Corp (XPCC) 
produced 1.85 MMT and non-XPCC farms produced 4.54 MMT, up 3.9 percent and 26.3 
percent, respectively, compared to last year.  
 
Another important data source is the China Fiber Quality Inspection Center (CFIC). The CFIC 
classifies Chinese cotton by grade and plays a key role in standardizing packaging and labeling 
of baled cotton, per the request of Cotton Quality Inspection System Reform Program initiated in 
2003. As of April 13, 2025, CFIC data revealed that the total volume of MY 24/25 classified 
cotton is approximately 6.79 MMT, of which 6.67 MMT is from Xinjiang. The gap between

The CNCE data and CFIC-classified data align closely when assessing MY 24/25 Xinjiang 
cotton production, each offering valuable insights from different perspectives. CNCE data better 
reflects cotton produced across all areas of the region, including potentially underreported 
marginal lands that may not be captured in NBS production surveys. CFIC-classified data 
provides a more comprehensive view of Xinjiang’s production since nearly all Xinjiang cotton 
undergoes classification, a mandatory step for transport outside the region and for receiving the 
subsidy. Together, CFIC-classified data and CNCE data complement each other, offering a 
comprehensive perspective on Xinjiang's cotton production and ensuring greater accuracy in 
tracking output across different regions. As of March 2025, both CNCE data and CFIC-classified 
data are significantly higher than the NBS estimate of 6.16 MMT. 
 
Conversely, relatively small volumes of cotton produced in other regions is classified, making 
CFIC a poor indicator of production outside of Xinjiang. Additionally, some farmers in these 
regions may sell cotton to cooperatives or mills that aren’t reporting their ginned volumes to 
CNCE. For this reason, NBS data may be considered as a more accurate source for production 
data outside of Xinjiang.

According to NBS data, Xinjiang’s share of cotton production continues to grow, reaching 92.6 
percent in MY 24/25, up from 90.9 percent in MY 23/24. Industry sources estimate a higher 
proportion of Xinjiang cotton production for MY 24/25, with BCO forecasting 6.49 MMT, 95.5 
percent of the national output. Xinjiang has benefited from a target-price subsidy since 2020, 
transportation subsidies, and relatively larger-scale farms that result in considerably higher yields 
compared with other regions. Due to higher labor costs, lower mechanization levels, lower 
prices, and a lack of subsidies, cotton farmers outside of Xinjiang experience higher production 
costs and much lower yields. A report published by the State Administration for Market 
Regulation indicated that the quality of Xinjiang cotton in 2024 reached its highest level in 
nearly six years in several indicators including fiber length, strength, and micronaire. As a result, 
the spinnability of Xinjiang cotton has significantly improved.

Planted Area 
 
Planted area for MY 25/26 is forecast at 2.93 Mha, unchanged from the previous marketing year.  
Forecast planted area in Xinjiang is 2.58 Mha, a slight increase of one percent compared with the 
previous year. This minor increase is primarily due to the price-target policy and the poor 
economic performance of other cash crops such as tomatoes that compete for planted area in the 
province. Planted area for all other cotton production regions is forecast at 0.35 Mha, down eight 
percent year-on-year, mainly attributed to the lower profits in MY 24/25 in all cotton producing 
regions outside of Xinjiang.  
 
Profitability and Planting Intentions 
While price movements in CY 2024 were relatively moderate, seed cotton prices have come 
down substantially since MY 23/24. According to the China Cotton Association (CCA), as of 
January 20, 2025, the national average selling price for seed cotton was 20.1 percent lower than 
that the previous year (see Table 3). Despite a moderate yield gain and stable production costs, 
the profitability of cotton production in Xinjiang is under pressure due to such a significant drop. 
Without the subsidy, sources suggest both machine-picked and hand-picked cotton on rented land 
would be unprofitable.

Several recent surveys of MY 25/26 cotton planting intentions point to a slight increase in total 
planted area, contrary to the trend observed in previous years. CCA forecasts a 0.4 percent 
increase in cotton planted area for MY 25/26 based on its March 2025 survey. Specifically, 
Xinjiang is expected to see a 1.8 percentage point increase, while the Yellow River and Yangtze 
River regions are projected to decline by 11.8 percent and 16.2 percent, respectively. The 
National Cotton Market Monitor System’s December 2024 Survey indicates a more 
significant increase of 1.9 percent in total cotton planting area. This includes a 3.2 percentage 
point increase in Xinjiang, offset by a 13.9 percent decrease in the Yellow River region and an 
8.0 percent decrease in the Yangtze River region. Another industry source corroborates this trend, 
which reported in early February a 0.8 percent increase in overall planting area, with Xinjiang 
contributing a 1.3 percent rise.  
 
All sources highlight a modest increase in China's overall cotton planting intentions for MY 
25/26, primarily driven by growth in Xinjiang, where government policies (See Subsidy section 
below) ensure stable returns despite falling crop prices. In contrast, the Yangtze and Yellow River 
regions show declines due to limited mechanization, higher labor costs, and lack of price support 
policies, with the National Monitoring System reporting the steepest drop in these regions. 
Several industry sources did share that the high concentration of cotton production in Xinjiang 
poses a challenge for industrial development and that to mitigate the risks, there should be efforts 
to gradually restore and maintain cotton production in inland areas. However, the latest surveys 
do not show any sign of the restoration. 
 
Spring planting has commenced in major cotton-growing regions such as Kashi (Kashgar), Aksu, 
and Korla of Xinjiang, with efforts focused on improving cotton quality using better seeds, 
advanced techniques, and modern machinery. According to the latest BCO survey, as of April 14, 
2025, cotton planting across Xinjiang has reached approximately 62.3 percent completion. 
Southern Xinjiang is entering the late planting stage with 66.6 percent completion and seedling 
emergence beginning at about 20.7 percent, while Northern and Eastern regions have entered 
intensive planting phases reaching 57.0 percent and 45.8 percent completion respectively. 
Southern Xinjiang planting is expected to be fully completed around April 25 as temperatures 
continue to rise, supporting the ongoing emergence of cotton seedlings across the region. 
Weather monitoring indicates that starting April 15, many areas in Northern Xinjiang will 
experience temperature drops, strong winds, and rainfall, which may impact planting progress 
despite the short duration of these weather events. 
 
Yields 
Post forecasts MY 25/26 cotton yield at 2,167 kg/ha assuming a return to trend, as the near-
perfect weather conditions in Xinjiang during MY 24/25 are unlikely to persist. According to 
NBS, cotton yields reached 2,171.6 kg/ha in MY 24/25 with higher yielding Xinjiang cotton 
reaching 2,323 kg/ha. Cotton yield estimates continue to vary by source depending on planted 
area and production estimates. In recent years, most sources indicate that yields have increased 
along with the rising proportion of Xinjiang’s share in planted area. 
 
Xinjiang’s higher yields compared to the national average demonstrate the region’s 
advantageous environment, large-scale farming enterprises, and high rates of mechanization. 
China continues to invest in cotton breeding and research and mentioned improving cotton

9 
 
quality as a goal in its 2025 Number One Document. Although Xinjiang farms under the 
umbrella of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corp (XPCC) have a higher rate of 
mechanization than non-XPCC farms, higher labor and other production costs have pushed the 
entire region to accelerate mechanization. Official media reports such as China Daily indicated 
that the mechanization rate for cotton planting in Xinjiang had reached 100 percent in 2024, and 
the mechanical harvesting rate stands at approximately 90 percent. Xinhua News also reported in 
January that, “The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region plans to strengthen its cotton industry as 
a pillar sector despite facing sanctions, according to the regional government work report in mid-
January.” It is then expected that Xinjiang is likely to continue promoting mechanization and 
technological advancements in cotton production.

Cotton yield in all other production areas outside of Xinjiang remains low. While Xinjiang’s 
yield is undoubtedly higher than other regions, official NBS data may overestimate the gap due 
to the mechanics of the PRC’s subsidy policy. Periods of high cotton prices incentivize farmers 
to expand onto marginal and lower yielding lands for which they are not eligible to receive 
subsidies. Official ginned and classified volumes in the region suggest farmers are likely 
underreporting planted area and claiming all harvested cotton originated from registered land 
(see Subsidy section below).  
 
Cotton Subsidies 
PRC subsidies for cotton production are a critical component of the government’s strategy to 
ensure a significant share of the cotton utilized by the world’s largest spinning and downstream 
textile and fabric manufacturing sector originates in China (i.e., supporting self-sufficiency 
campaigns). The subsides also serve the purpose of ensuring a stable income to millions of 
cotton farmers, especially in Xinjiang. PRC cotton subsidies can generally be divided into two 
categories: those for Xinjiang and those for other provinces. The broad outlines of the subsidies 
provided to Xinjiang cotton are generally understood in terms of scope and purpose. Subsidies 
provided to other provinces are less clear, as these appear to be applied at provincial and sub-
provincial levels and involve much lower amounts.

In February 2025, the PRC released its No. 1 Document (link in Chinese, for more information 
please see GAIN CH2025-0048), an annual policy document focused on agriculture and rural 
development. In Section 1.1, the document emphasized the need to “promote the stable 
production and quality improvement of cotton, sugar crops, natural rubber, and other related 
products.” Additionally, MARA outlined an implementation plan (link in Chinese) for the No. 1 
Document, which included measures to “stabilize domestic cotton supply” and “effectively 
implement the cotton target price policy while consolidating Xinjiang’s advantages in cotton 
production.” On April 2, 2025, the General Office of the Central Committee of CCP and the 
General Office of the State Council jointly issued the Opinions on Improving the Price 
Governance Mechanism (link in Chinese). This document highlighted that the government will 
“optimize the target price policy for cotton,” signaling that this policy will remain in effect 
during the upcoming market year of MY 25/26. 
 
Xinjiang Subsidy 
The target price-based subsidy for Xinjiang cotton was established in MY 17/18 (see GAIN 
report CH18014). On April 14, 2023, the PRC announced an extension of the program for three 
years, from MY 23/34 through MY 25/26, with a fixed target price of 18,600 yuan/MT 
($2,650/MT) and reduced the production cap entitled to subsidy to 5.1 MMT from the previous 
5.4 MMT. The stability of planting intentions in Xinjiang in recent years is tightly linked to the 
PRC’s target-price subsidy policy for that region (see GAIN report Cotton Subsidy Policy 
Updated).  
 
Cotton subsidy payments are distributed directly to farmers by local government offices, usually 
between November and March. In MY 24/25, the price index (CC Index 3128B) average selling 
price in the first seven months was 15,056 yuan/MT ($2,077/MT). Based on NBS’s production 
number for Xinjiang, the total MY 24/25 subsidy payout for the region is expected to be 
approximately 17.3 billion yuan ($2.39 billion).

The PRC also provides subsidies to transport Xinjiang cotton to mills outside the region. In 
recent years, the subsidy provided approximately 500 yuan/MT ($70/MT) for cotton and cotton 
yarn shipped from Xinjiang to other parts of China. However, the subsidy amount has been 
reduced to 300 yuan/MT ($41/MT) in 2022 and furtherly reduced to 200 yuan/MT ($28/MT) in 
September 2024 to support the development of the spinning industry inside Xinjiang. A separate 
transport subsidy established in 2022 covers yarn products shipped from the region, ranging from 
600 yuan/MT ($83/MT) to 900 yuan/MT ($124/MT) in 2022 and was adjusted to a new range 
from 500 yuan/MT ($69/MT) to 640 yuan/MT ($88/MT) in 2024. The amount is based on yarn 
varieties and production location. The subsidy is claimed on transport records or bills of lading

certified by government agencies. Payments are typically provided to the enterprises the 
following year. These changes in transport subsidies are part of a broader policy to increase 
Xinjiang's cotton-textile conversion rate to 45 percent by 2028, up from 40 percent in 2024. 
 
In addition to the transport subsidy, the local government provided quality-based subsidies 
starting in 2024. The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Development and Reform 
Commission announced in its Implement Program (link in Chinese) that, the autonomous region 
will increase policy support for high-quality cotton production, implementing quality subsidies in 
all cotton-producing counties (cities, districts) across the region. The total quality subsidy will be 
about five percent of the target-price subsidy funds for cotton in the current calendar year. 
  
Subsides for Other Provinces 
An article (link in Chinese) published by cncotton.com on February 14, 2023, describes PRC 
cotton subsidies for provinces other than Xinjiang as follows: 
 
"From MY 2014/15, the subsidy rate is 2,000 yuan/MT ($280/MT), and the 
subsidy amount per MT in the following years will be calculated based on 60 
percent of Xinjiang's target price subsidy standard, with an upper limit of 2,000 
yuan/MT. The central government subsidizes these cotton-producing provinces 
based on NBS production data. The subsidy method is determined by each 
province independently, and it can choose to subsidize by area or by production.” 
 
Thus, the central government provides the funds to provincial authorities who develop their own 
plans to distribute payments in their respective provinces, which may include additional local-
level subsidies. Official reports regarding the distribution of the subsidy payments are not readily 
available. However, total payments to farmers in other regions are understood to be significantly 
lower than their Xinjiang counterparts. 
 
In addition to the aforementioned direct subsidy, the Agricultural Insurance Premium Subsidy 
Management Measures (link in Chinese) developed by the Ministry of Finance (MOF) is 
available to cotton growers. This program aims to cover part of the expenses for full-cost 
insurance1 and planting-income insurance,2 available in nation-wide planting of grain crops, 
including cotton. Beneficiaries of this subsidy include “farmers and agricultural production 
associations, encompassing moderately scaled farmers and small household farmers.” The 
central government provides additional subsidies to cover the insurance costs of beneficiaries 
nationwide, with specific subsidy rates varying depending on the insurance subsidies provided 
by provincial governments in different regions. Overall, the combined provincial and central 
government subsidies can cover approximately 70 to 80 percent of the crop insurance costs. On 
March 18, 2025, MARA released the 2025 Central Government Subsidy Policies for 
Strengthening, Benefiting, and Enriching Agriculture (link in Chinese), which confirmed the 
continued availability of the insurance cost subsidy on cotton. The subsidy funding will be 
allocated to different provinces, where they develop their own plan to distribute the payments.

The sum amount insured3 from insurance program of each province vary and is usually not 
public. Limited accessible data shows that in the central provinces, the amount insured is usually 
between 5,250 to 6,000 yuan per hectare ($729 to $833 per hectare). It is difficult to find out how 
many farmers are incentivized by the subsidy to plant cotton and join in crop insurance plans. 
 
Consumption 
 
Post forecasts MY 25/26 cotton consumption at 8.15 MMT on continued, moderate domestic 
economic growth, as well as potentially diversified overseas demand for textile and apparel 
products. Post estimated MY 24/25 consumption at 8.05 MMT as competitive domestic cotton 
prices have bolstered domestic spinning and forecast potential growth in domestic demand for 
textile and apparel products in the latter half of the marketing year. 
 
Estimates of MY 24/25 cotton use by industry sources vary from 7.69 MMT to 8.15 MMT. All 
sources indicate an increasing consumption compared to MY 23/24. BCO is still the only source 
forecasting MY 25/26 cotton use, at 8.1 MMT, a slight decline from its estimate for MY 24/25.

Administrative Measures of State Cotton Reserve 
On January 30, 2024, the PRC published The Administrative Measures of State Cotton Reserve 
(link in Chinese) which took effect on April 1, 2024. The measures specify management 
practices for state cotton reserves in terms of purchase, rotation/sales, and use. The National 
Food and Strategic Reserves Administration is responsible for the overall management of state 
cotton reserves. The Ministry of Finance is responsible for formulating financial subsidy policy 
for the state cotton reserves and disbursing subsidy funds. Taken as a whole, the measures 
provide a general framework for the operations and management of state cotton reserves. 
 
The measures, for the first time, establish a period of 5 years, in principle, for the rotation of state 
cotton reserves. Additionally, the measures specify conditions for purchases of domestic cotton 
for state reserves, including:  
o cotton supply significantly exceeds demand or cotton price falls rapidly and significantly 
in domestic market;  
o the central cotton reserve volume is lower than the “reserve scale;” and  
o the State Council considers it necessary to purchase cotton for reserves under other 
conditions.  
The measures also specify conditions for utilization of state cotton reserves, including:  
o cotton supply falls short of demand or cotton price increase rapidly and significantly in 
domestic market;  
o use of state cotton reserve is needed in case of natural disasters or other emergency and 
national defense mobilization; and  
o the State Council considers it necessary to use the state cotton reserve under other 
conditions. 
 
Notably, the measures do not provide a definition for “reserve scale.” 
 
U.S. Restrictions on Xinjiang Cotton 
On December 23, 2021, the United States signed The Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act 
(UFLPA) into law. The UFLPA creates a rebuttable presumption that goods entering the United 
States from the PRC, produced wholly or in part, in Xinjiang are made with forced labor, as well 
as certain goods made by entities elsewhere in the PRC that use forced labor by members of 
persecuted groups from Xinjiang. Starting on June 21, 2022, U.S. Customs and Border 
Protection (CBP) began to implement the UFLPA’s provisions. For additional information please 
see the CBP UFLPA Fact Sheet and Operational Guidance for Importers. Statistics on 
enforcement of the UFLPA can be found here. 
 
In response to the law, at the 2024 Chinese People’s Political Consultative Committee (CPPCC), 
an advisory body supervised by the Chinese Communist Party and not the PRC government, a 
senior Xinjiang cotton industry leader proposed the establishment of a common cotton market 
under the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) framework to expand the market for

25 
 
Xinjiang cotton and cotton products. The proposal aims to reduce the world's reliance on U.S. 
and Australian cotton, offset the effects of the UFLPA, and allow China to share its cotton 
production and processing technologies with member states. 
 
The Xinjiang Cotton Subsidy Policy 
In April 2023, China announced a target price for Xinjiang cotton at 18,600 yuan/MT 
($2,650/MT) for the period 2023 to 2025 and capped the volume of Xinjiang cotton entitled to 
subsidy at 5.1 MMT annually, down from 5.4 MMT in previous years (see GAIN Report Cotton 
Subsidy Policy Updated for additional information). Implementation details were announced by 
the Xinjiang Autonomous Region government in July 2023 (see GAIN Report Cotton and 
Products Update for additional information). 
 
On February 28, 2024, in a document to all provincial governments on “Implementation 
Opinions on Promoting the Deployment of Comprehensive Rural Revitalization” (link in 
Chinese), MARA highlighted plans to “implement a policy linking cotton target price subsidies 
with cotton quality.” The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Development and Reform 
Commission announced in its Implementing Program that the autonomous region will increase 
policy support for high-quality cotton production, implementing quality subsidies in all cotton-
producing counties (cities, districts) across the region. The total quality subsidy will be about 5 
percent of the target-price subsidy funds for cotton in the current calendar year. It also clarified 
that after 2024 (and in 2025), cotton grown using the fruit-cotton intercropping model will no 
longer be eligible for subsidies, encouraging the concentration of cotton cultivation in designated 
production protection zones. With regard to the 5-percent quality subsidy, in September 2024, the 
Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Market Supervision and Administration Bureau released an 
official notice detailing the implementation plan for the quality subsidy. The notice and its 
associated explanations specified that the quality subsidy standard in Xinjiang would be 
approximately 350 yuan per metric ton in 2024 and 2025. Only classified seed cotton meeting 
specific quality standards (see below) will be eligible for this subsidy. 
 
o Fiber length: ≥ 29mm 
o Fiber strength: ≥ 29 cN/tex 
o Micronaire: A grade or B2 grade 
o Length uniformity index: ≥ 82% 
 
Targeted Loans  
The Agriculture Development Bank of China (ADBC) continues to provide loans at favorable 
terms to traders and gin operators for seed cotton purchases. Media reports indicated ADBC 
provided 43.7 billion yuan ($6.16 billion) in loans as of the end of 2023, up 22.5 percent year-
on-year, to help purchase Xinjiang cotton. The increase in loan values is partly attributable to 
higher prices for seed cotton. ADBC claims the loans facilitate cotton marketing and stable 
cotton production in Xinjiang. 
 
Registration System for Overseas Cotton Suppliers  
Before exporting cotton to China, overseas cotton suppliers must register with GACC. U.S. 
cotton exporters should work with their China-based representatives or customers to complete 
the registration process via the online system at

http://online.customs.gov.cn/static/pages/alllistitems.html. Registrations are valid for five years 
and may be renewed. GACC publishes a list of recent registration approvals and renewals on its 
website. The lists were most recently updated October 31, 2024. 
 
Section 301 Retaliatory Tariffs Exclusion Process  
Beginning March 2, 2020, the PRC implemented a tariff exclusion process for Section 301 
retaliatory tariffs on U.S. cotton (see GAIN report CH2020-0024). Currently, tariff exclusions 
continue to be processed for both state-owned and non-state-owned enterprises. 
 
Cotton Standard Enforced on September 1, 2024 
National Standard on Cotton—Part 1: Saw Ginned Upland Cotton GB 1103.1-2023 came into 
force on September 1, 2024. The National Standard on Cotton—Part 2: Roller Ginned Upland 
Cotton GB 1103.2-2012 remain unchanged. 
 
The new GB 1103.1-2023 introduced short fiber content as a new indicator, added automated 
impurity testing and manual foreign fiber detection methods, introduced QR code labeling, 
tightened standards for official impurity content and ginning quality, improved sampling 
representativeness, and maintained stability in color grade, micronaire, length, and strength 
indicators. These changes aim to improve cotton quality, adapt to new industry trends, and meet 
modern market demands in China's cotton sector. 
 
Cotton China Sustainable Development Program  
CCA initiated the “Cotton China Sustainable Development Program” (CCSD) on April 30, 2021. 
As of October 2023, 30 domestic enterprises engaged in cotton production and related industries 
had signed onto the program (See more in GAIN Report Cotton and Products Update ). In an 
effort to further promote the program, on October 8, 2023, the CCA held the second CCSD 
sustainable cotton on-site exchange meeting in Korla City, Xinjiang. The meeting featured nearly 
200 participants from government, cotton spinning enterprises, and media and included a visit to 
a CCSD demonstration farm. This program continued in the following year, on December 4, 
2024, CCA organized a training on CCSD in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, with over 40 
participants from both associations and member companies.
